items.title: ClawMoat – Open-source runtime security for AI agents (zero deps, <1ms)

I built ClawMoat because I run AI agents on my laptop with access to my SSH keys, AWS credentials, and browser data. The agents are useful but terrifying — one prompt injection away from exfiltrating everything. • Secret scanning — catches API keys, tokens, credentials before they leak
• PII protection — SSN, credit cards, emails
• Host Guardian — 4 permission tiers (observer/worker/standard/full), forbidden zones protecting ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, browser credentials, crypto wallets
• Inter-agent message scanning — detects impersonation, concealment, and privilege escalation between agents
• Policy engine — YAML-based rules

items.title: 清华刘洋团队论文：揭示为何 70B 的医疗模型，反而不如 8B 会问诊丨ILCR 2026
items.raw_excerpt: 在医疗人工智能的发展历程中，能力评估方式在很大程度上塑造了技术演进的方向。 过去相当长一段时间里，医疗 AI 的进步主要围绕医学知识获取与推理展开，模型是否“足够聪明”通常通过医学考试题、临床问答数据集等静态基准来衡量。在这一评价框架下，模型只需在信息完整、问题封闭的条件下给出正确答案，便被视为具备较高的医疗能力。 随着大语言模型的兴起，这一路径迅速取得突破性进展，多种系统在 MedQA 等测试中达到甚至超过人类专家水平，使得“医疗 AI 是否已经成熟”一度成为行业内的乐观判断。 然而，随着这些模型被逐步引入更贴近真实临床的交互场景，一个长期被掩盖的问题开始显现：真实医疗实践并非基于完整信息给出诊断，而是一种在高度不确定条件下，通过连续提问、风险识别与信息整合来逐步逼近决策的动态过程。 模型在静态评测中展现出的知识优势，并未自然转化为对真实问诊场景的可靠支持，反而在多轮对话中暴露出提问策略僵化、对高风险信号反应迟钝、过早形成结论以及缺乏基本沟通与共情能力等缺陷。 这种“高分通过考试，却难以胜任临床问诊”的断层，逐渐成为医疗 AI 领域的核心瓶颈，也迫使研究者重新思考一个根本性问题：医疗智能体真正需要被训练和评估的，究竟是什么能力。 在这一背景下，清华大学刘洋团队提出了题为《DOCTOR-R1: Mastering Clinical Inquiry with Experiential Agentic Reinforcement Learning》的研究工作，试图从问题建模和训练范式层面打破以静态知识评测为中心的既有路径。 这项研究不再将模型能力简单等同于知识覆盖度或参数规模，而是将临床问诊本身视为一个长期、多轮、部分可观测且高度风险敏感的决策过程，重点探索如何让模型学会在信息不完整的条件下提出高价值问题、动态调整询问策略，并在整个过程中保持安全意识与沟通质量。为医疗智能体从工

For a considerable period, progress in medical AI primarily revolved around the acquisition and reasoning of medical knowledge, with models' "intelligence" often measured by static benchmarks such as medical exam questions and clinical Q&A datasets. Under this evaluation framework, models were considered to possess high medical capability as long as they provided correct answers under conditions of complete information and closed questions. With the rise of large language models, this approach quickly achieved breakthroughs, with multiple systems reaching or surpassing human expert levels in tests like MedQA, leading to optimistic industry assessments about whether "medical AI has matured." However, as these models were gradually introduced into interactive scenarios closer to real clinical practice, a long-overlooked issue emerged: real medical practice is not about making diagnoses based on complete information but a dynamic process of gradually approaching decisions through continuous questioning, risk identification, and information integration under conditions of high uncertainty. Author: Wu You  Editor: Yu Kuai  
The 2026 CCTV Spring Festival Gala reached a historic high in "tech content," with collective pushes from three major sectors: AI, robotics, and consumer electronics. Frequent appearances were made not only by Volcano Engine, Doubao, Bilibili, and Xiaohongshu, but also by deep involvement from embodied intelligence companies like Magic Atom, Songyan Power, Galaxy General, and Yushu. The Spring Festival Gala is transforming from a nationwide cultural feast into a must-win battleground for brands.  
According to CCTV News data, one day after the 2025 Spring Festival Gala aired, it accumulated 16.8 billion impressions across all media. The CCTV Spring Festival Gala is almost the only communication scenario that achieves full-age, full-region, and full-scenario coverage, representing the ceiling of national-level traffic.  
Securing a spot on the Spring Festival Gala partnership list is no easy task. Interestingly, this year’s Gala selected the official cooperative earphones, MOVA TPEAK Clip Pro, which come from MOVA TPEAK—an emerging audio brand established less than two years ago. MOVA TPEAK is a representative brand of MOVA’s ecosystem company, Lingjie Qidian. Both MOVA and MOVA TPEAK are certified as official consumer electronics strategic partners of the "2026 CCTV Spring Festival Gala."  
MOVA TPEAK’s appearance not only broke the long-standing dominance of traditional consumer goods like alcohol and milk on the Spring Festival Gala stage but also signaled that Chinese smart hardware brands have entered a new phase.

Author: Wu You  Editor: Yu Kuai  
If evaluating the market acceptance of an AI hardware product by its crowdfunding amount, one million dollars is a threshold. Surpassing this figure indicates that product-market fit is essentially viable, signaling the birth of another hit product.  

The AI card phone MindOne, which garnered significant attention at CES 2026, was launched on Kickstarter in July last year. Priced starting at $299, it attracted support from 3,411 backers worldwide. Within 30 days of its release, it raised approximately $1.48 million. Supporters expressed interest in its portability, AI features, and retro design.  

MindOne’s card-style design is compact and lightweight, with a thickness of 8.9mm and a weight of 136g, appealing to many users who pursue a minimalist lifestyle. Its 50-megapixel Sony main camera, along with a 180-degree reversible camera design, is also considered a highlight.  

In terms of AI functionality, the device features dual-system switching between Android 15 and iKKO AI OS. Users can switch to AI OS focus mode with one click, enabling offline AI functions such as real-time translation, speech-to-text, and image analysis to enhance efficiency.  

For expandability, the detachable keyboard case brings back the "BlackBerry" era, receiving widespread acclaim from tech enthusiasts and retro aficionados.  

Just last week, iKKO completed its domestic debut at the INNO100 offline experience store in Shenzhen, accelerating its expansion into the Chinese market ahead of the Spring Festival.  

"Our primary targets are Europe, the United States, Japan, and Southeast Asia, with our user base covering white-collar professionals."

Author: Wu You  Editor: Yu Kuai  
Shortly after the 2023 Spring Festival holiday ended, employees at Teeni.AI received a company-wide notice from CEO Yuan Lin: "All business shifts to AI, focusing fully on youth-oriented intelligent agents." This decision stemmed from an intuition born of her dual identity—she is both a serial entrepreneur deeply involved in the children’s hardware sector and a mother of two children born in the 2010s.  

A decade ago, during her first entrepreneurial venture, Yuan Lin’s product, Pudding Doudou, belonged to the AI 1.0 era. The team initially developed an OS system before targeting the children’s market, but the AI technology at the time "could only fool kids." The most popular feature was using the robot as a "messenger" to bridge communication between parents and children, which formed her initial understanding of children’s needs.  

Her second venture, Listening Bear, originally focused on English learning scenarios. It wasn’t until the explosion of GPT technology, watching her own children skillfully use AI to search for information and ask questions, that Yuan Lin suddenly realized: "This wave of opportunity cannot be missed." She immediately halted the original plans, led the training of a dedicated large model for youth, and launched an AI portable intelligent agent.  

Her experience of speaking with thousands of children each year helped her grasp the core of interacting with the post-2010 generation: "You have to squat down and speak their language; respect is more important than anything." She sharply pointed out a common industry flaw—many AI companion hardware products rely on generic models with forced personas. In her view, AI should not play an omnipotent role but should serve as a "cognitive bridge," helping children connect the virtual and physical worlds.

Justo después de las vacaciones del Año Nuevo chino de 2023, los empleados de Teeni.AI recibieron una notificación de su CEO, Yuan Lin: "Todas las operaciones se orientarán hacia la IA, centrándonos al máximo en los agentes inteligentes para adolescentes." Detrás de esta decisión hay una intuición derivada de su doble identidad: es tanto una emprendedora en serie con profunda experiencia en el sector de hardware infantil como madre de dos hijos nacidos después de 2010. En su primer emprendimiento hace diez años, su producto Pudding Doudou aún estaba en la era de la IA 1.0. El equipo primero desarrolló un sistema operativo y luego se enfocó en el sector infantil, pero la tecnología de IA de entonces "solo podía engañar a los niños". La función más popular era hacer que el robot actuara como "mensajero".
